ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$. If $\angle ADC = 140^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$, and $\angle ADC=140^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle ABC=40^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle AOC=2\angle ABC=80^\circ$,\\
Hence, $\angle AOC=\boxed{80^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: A, B, C, and D are all on the same circle, with O marked as the center and radii OA and OC drawn, so ∠AOC is the central angle subtending chord/arc AC. From the text, use ∠ADC = 140°. Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠ABC = 180° - 140° = 40°. Then ∠ABC is an inscribed angle subtending arc AC, while ∠AOC is the central angle subtending the same arc AC. Apply the rule that a central angle is twice the corresponding inscribed angle: ∠AOC = 2 × 40° = 80°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: points A, D, C lie along the upper part of the circle, B lies on the lower part, and O is the center with OA and OC forming the smaller central angle ∠AOC. From the text, ∠ADC = 140°. The inscribed angle ∠ADC intercepts the arc AC that does not contain D, which is the large lower arc passing through B. By the inscribed-angle theorem, that intercepted arc has measure 2 × 140° = 280°. The full circle is 360°, so the remaining minor arc AC measures 360° - 280° = 80°.
